title: the words before every beginning
hook: the words before every beginning — a meal, a drive, an exam
tomorrow: what your prayer is actually saying

segments.voice: Before the first bite of dinner. Before the car pulls out of the driveway. At the top of an exam, before the first answer. Under the breath, fast, so it's easy to miss: bismillah. Many Muslims have said it since before they could read. It goes before a beginning, so it goes first here too. First, a guess.
screen: `BEFORE THE FIRST BITE.` → `BEFORE THE CAR PULLS OUT.` → `BISMILLAH.`

segments.voice: Bismillah is three pieces. Bi: in, or with. Ism: name. Allah: God. In the name of God. Allah isn't the name of a separate god; it's the Arabic word for God, and Arabic-speaking Christians and Jews say it too. The full line is bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim: “In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.” All but one of the Qur'an's chapters, called surahs, open with it. So what does it do? Starting in someone's name means you're not starting alone. It's like working under a name you respect: the work carries that name now, so you want it to be worth carrying. That's why it goes before small things, not only big ones. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ once told a boy eating beside him: say bismillah, and eat with your right hand. And for the times you forget, because everyone does, another of his sayings gives a way back in: say it when you remember, in the name of God, at its beginning and its end. Nobody gets locked out of their own lunch.
screen: `BI — IN. ISM — NAME. ALLAH — GOD.` · `ALL BUT ONE SURAH OPENS WITH IT.` · `YOU'RE NOT STARTING ALONE.` · `FORGOT? SAY IT WHEN YOU REMEMBER.`

segments.voice: One breath with the bell. Think of the very next thing you'll do after this: coffee, an email, the car. Breathe in. On the way out, say the word for it, aloud or under your breath: bismillah. Or simply give it one full pause before it begins.
Bismillah. In the name of God: the words before a beginning, so nothing starts alone. First word on your strand.

howItsDone: Muslims say bismillah before eating, drinking, setting out, studying and many small daily tasks, and the full line, bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim, is recited before reading the Qur'an.

story.title: the letter a bird delivered
story.text: A bird turns up late to King Solomon's court with news: a queen in the land of Sheba, rich and powerful, and her people bowing to the sun. Solomon writes her a letter and sends the bird to drop it in front of her. She calls her nobles together. A noble letter has been thrown to me, she says. It's from Solomon, and it begins: in the name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
story.source: Qur'an 27:20–31 (the hoopoe and the queen of Sheba; the bismillah at 27:30)

wrong.myth: bismillah is a grace said before meals.
wrong.truth: it means in the name of God, and it goes before almost any beginning: a meal, a drive, an exam, a hard conversation.
